summary:
This tutorial introduces Mozilla Thunderbird, a simple email client available for various platforms. It covers downloading and launching Thunderbird, configuring new email accounts, reading, writing, and sending emails, and logging out. Thunderbird supports multiple email accounts like Gmail and Yahoo, allowing you to manage them on your local computer. For Ubuntu Linux 12.04, you can install Thunderbird via the Software Center or download it directly from the website. Thunderbird works with POP3 and IMAP protocols, enabling you to download emails and manage different accounts efficiently.

To set up an email account in Thunderbird, ensure it's POP3-enabled and connected to the internet. Launch Thunderbird by clicking the Thunderbird icon on the desktop. Open the Mail Account Setup dialog, configure the account, and then launch Thunderbird. The interface includes a main menu with options like Get Mail, Write, and Address Book. Thunderbird displays folders from your configured accounts on the left panel and advanced features on the right panel. For this tutorial, two email accounts (stuserone@gmail.com and stusertwo@yahoo.com) were set up with POP3 enabled. Follow similar steps for other email providers to configure Thunderbird effectively.
